title: Multiple intron motifs have redundant functions in the trans-splicing of the mod(mdg4) locus.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and read the only processed file in GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE302152: GSE302152_splice_junction_counts.txt.gz, 284 bytes gzipped, 28 data rows (27 mod(mdg4) isoforms plus one intron3 row) x 4 columns (3 mutant replicates, 1 wild-type sample), with blank cells for undetected junctions. Read the GEO series record: 4 samples total, Drosophila melanogaster. Listed all 37 files in PRIDE (proteomics repository) project PXD079014 via its API: 6 mass-spectrometry runs as .raw/.mgf/.mzid/.tandem.xml search outputs (0.9-1.3 GB each raw) plus a 2,285-byte experimental-design sheet; no processed protein quantification table. Read the paper's data availability and methods sections.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The reporter-construct deletion series (how many transgenic constructs were measured and their trans-splicing efficiencies) is described in the text and figures only; I could not retrieve the supplementary tables because the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice (supplement not retrievable). Supplementary Table S4 is said to hold the retained proteomics hits, and S2 the fly stocks, but I did not see them.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO GSE302152 and PRIDE PXD079014 are both public with no login; I fetched the GEO processed file and the PRIDE file list. Only the article supplement was unreachable (endpoint timeouts).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The quantity of interest, trans-splicing efficiency per intron variant, is not a deposited column: it exists only as bar charts in the figures for each reporter construct. The one deposited table holds raw junction read counts for 27 isoforms, from which a ratio would have to be constructed, and only for two genotypes.

a3_inputs_present.note: Input sequences (the 600 bp intron 4 region, the deletion variants) are obtainable from the Drosophila genome and the figures, so inputs are not the blocker.

a4_units_stated.note: The deposited file is plainly labelled as splice junction read counts per isoform per sample; units are unambiguous even though no header documentation is given.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified in the file: 28 rows x 4 samples = 112 count values total, from 4 RNA-seq libraries. The reporter experiments add only tens of constructs. This is two to three orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row threshold.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 MB processed; ~10 GB if raw mass-spectrometry files were ever needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed data is a 284-byte gzipped text file; trivially fits. Raw proteomics would be ~10 GB but is not needed and exceeds the download cap.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO's stated design (3 mutant replicates vs wild-type, isoform-level junction comparison) matches the 4 columns and 27 isoform rows I opened; no conflicting counts found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Counts come directly from sequencing reads at splice junctions, not from any model's output, so provenance is a physical measurement. This killer is not the problem here.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: with 27 isoform rows from two genotypes and tens of reporter constructs quantified only in figures, any model would describe one locus in one species with no held-out groups.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use intron sequence variants to predict how efficiently two separate transcripts are joined into one messenger RNA.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: each reporter construct's intron 4 sequence (deletions, inversions, motif swaps of a 600 base-pair region) as input. Verified example count is far too small: 28 rows in the one deposited table and tens of constructs described in the text.
plain_idea.predict: Trans-splicing efficiency, that is the fraction of transcripts in which a 5' donor exon set is joined to a 3' exon from a separately transcribed pre-messenger RNA. Measured by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR and by RNA-seq junction counts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups engineering trans-splicing for RNA therapeutics would value sequence rules for when two transcripts join, and the specific question has no existing model; but this paper does not supply enough measurements to learn any rule.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: learn trans-splicing efficiency from intron 4 sequence variants, using a DNA/RNA language model such as HyenaDNA or RNA-FM as a frozen backbone with a regression head. The idea is genuinely unmodelled, but the paper supplies only a single locus, two genotypes and a handful of engineered constructs, so there is nothing to train on.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual downloaded file (284 bytes gzipped, 28 rows); nothing here is compute-limited, it is data-limited.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the single GEO processed file. I did: 28 rows x 4 samples, which kills it in one command.

verdict_reason: Verified in the files: the only deposited quantitative table has 28 rows across 4 samples (A5 fails badly), and the trans-splicing efficiencies for the deletion constructs, the paper's real measurements, exist only in figures rather than as a column (A2 fails). The proteomics deposit is 6 raw mass-spectrometry runs with no processed protein table. A careful single-locus molecular genetics study, not an ML dataset.
